cases.description: Earlier peak-quality mucus patches dry up, then a later true Peak Day appears.
cases.label: Repeat false peaks before true Peak Day

cases.description: Long follicular phase with Peak Day much later than calendar-day assumptions.
cases.label: Late ovulation in a long cycle

cases.description: Third high is above the coverline but below the 0.2 C threshold; fourth high is needed.
cases.label: Slow staircase temperature rise

cases.description: Third high lands exactly on coverline + 0.2 C and should confirm without day four.
cases.label: Exact 0.2 C third-high threshold

cases.description: One of the first three high temperatures is disturbed and cannot be counted.
cases.label: Disturbed high temperature blocks confirmation

cases.description: A missing day interrupts the required consecutive 6-low/3-high temperature sequence.
cases.label: Missing calendar day blocks temperature confirmation

cases.description: A later fever-like reading is charted after the true shift and should be warned on.
cases.label: Fever/elevated temperature warning

cases.description: No mucus observations are recorded; Peak Day should stay empty and the unclear-mucus exception should be used for BBT.
cases.label: No mucus observations, temperature-only confirmation

cases.description: A valid-looking early rise occurs before a later Peak Day; highs after Peak Day should be used.
cases.label: Premature pre-Peak temperature rise is ignored

cases.description: Internal medium bleeding appears without a confirmed temperature shift.
cases.label: Breakthrough bleeding without ovulatory shift

cases.description: The chart ends on a peak-quality day, so there is no later lower-quality day to lock Peak Day.
cases.label: Peak-quality mucus at chart end is not locked

sources.label: WHO multicentre ovulation method study
sources.note: Cycle length mean 28.5 days, SD 3.18; mucus Peak Day mean day 15, SD 2.6.

sources.label: Fehring 2002 Peak Day study
sources.note: Peak Day was within +/-4 days of estimated ovulation in 97.8% of compared cycles.

sources.label: NCBI StatPearls BBT physiology
sources.note: Follicular BBT commonly sits around 97.0-98.0 F; luteal rise is about 0.5-1.0 F.

sources.label: Frank-Herrmann/Sensiplan paper
sources.note: Temperature rise rule: three highs over previous six, with the last high 0.2 C above the previous six.

sources.label: Bailey and Marshall luteal phase summary
sources.note: Hyperthermic phase commonly around 10-13 days across shorter to typical cycle lengths.
